task_instance: Given a small sample C program (source text created in the work directory), use the dwarf-expert skill's core workflow to analyze the DWARF debug info of the compiled binary: compile it with debug info, then run llvm-dwarfdump/dwarfdump (or readelf --debug-dump) to list DW_TAG_subprogram DIEs and their DW_AT_ attributes.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is inspecting DWARF debug info inside a compiled binary via dwarfdump/llvm-dwarfdump/readelf, or by running a pyelftools/libdwarf/gimli script against such a binary. This office-assistant runtime cannot run any code, scripts, or shell commands (no Bash tool at all), cannot compile source into a binary, and cannot produce/read binary files (ELF/Mach-O executables or .o/.dSYM). Every path through the skill (running dwarfdump/readelf, running --verify or --statistics, or writing and executing a pyelftools script) requires code execution and a binary artifact, both of which are outside the granted abilities (text file read/write/edit and web fetch/search only). I wrote a sample C source file (sample.c) as the input a user would supply, but could not compile it, could not obtain or fabricate a real compiled binary with genuine DWARF sections, and was not permitted to run any DWARF tool or fabricate the tool's output. The only sub-parts of the skill reachable in this runtime (looking up DWARF standard facts via WebSearch/WebFetch on dwarfstd.org, or writing an unexecuted/unverified pyelftools script as inert text) are not the skill's core stated deliverable of actually analyzing/verifying DWARF info in a binary.
